module: Shared editor tools for placing, selecting, moving and undoing forest items (Forest / ForestData), extracted from forestEditor.lua so that a second tool (the parallax interior editor) reuses the same mechanics. Everything is parameterized by the `forest`/`forestData` handle (no scene state in the module); the selection is the global store `editor.selection.forestItem`, and modifications go through `editor.history` (undoable). Also contains the packing of the per-instance data of the "parallax" windows (32-bit integer customData) and filters on the `parallax_` prefix of ForestItemData datablocks.
usage:
-- in a tool's onUpdate:
local tools = require("editor/api/forestItemTools")
tools.updateSelectMode(forest, tools.isParallaxItem)
tools.handleGizmo(forest)
notes: The module is a regular `require` that returns M; it depends on an already initialized global `editor` (editor.createForestItem, editor.updateForestItem, editor.history, axis gizmo).

Parallax customData: bits 0-23 = texture set id (0xFFFFFF = none/disabled), bits 24-31 = flags (bit 0 = emissive). Value < 0 = disabled and not saved on the C++ side. Must stay in sync with shaders/common/examples/parallaxInterior.h.hlsl.
Shift at the start of a gizmo drag arms a duplicate: the clone is only created on the first drag frame, and everything is recorded as a single "AddForestItems" action (undo = deletion of the clones).
In scale mode, the gizmo adds at most 0.1 per frame to each item's uniform scale.
`removeItems` does nothing (returns nil) if the list is empty; `addItems`/`removeItems` return the result of commitAction.

PARALLAX_ITEM_PREFIX.desc: "parallax_" prefix of the name (or internalName) of a ForestItemData datablock identifying a parallax window; the parallax editor only touches these items, the forest editor the others.

getSelection.desc: Returns the current selection of forest items (editor.selection.forestItem) or an empty table.

clearSelection.desc: Deselects all selected forest items, rebuilds the instance data and clears the selection.

select.desc: Selects the given items (nil or empty = clear). Places the axis gizmo (on the item in local mode with a single item, otherwise on the centroid), rebuilds the instances and emits onEditorObjectSelectionChanged. Does not trigger the forest editor's mesh preview.

addItems.desc: Adds items in an undoable way ("AddForestItems" action); redo selects the added items.

dontCallRedo.desc: true if the items already exist (does not run the redo); default false

removeItems.desc: Removes items in an undoable way ("RemoveForestItems" action). Does nothing if the list is empty.

dontCallRedo.desc: true = do not execute now; default false

place.desc: Instantiates an item from a datablock at the given transform and returns the final handle. Does NOT record history: the caller commits (typically via addItems). afterCreate can modify the new item (e.g. parallax customData) and return the final handle to keep.

pick.desc: Returns the forest item rendered under the mouse (camera-mouse ray), or nil; filterFn can reject items that don't belong to the tool.

handleGizmo.desc: Drives and draws the axis gizmo for the current selection (translation with terrain snapping, rotation around the centroid, uniform scale, duplication via Shift). Records the undoable "SetForestItemTransform" action (or "AddForestItems" for a duplicate) at the end of the drag. To be called once per frame from the tool's onUpdate. Does nothing without a selection.

updateSelectMode.desc: One frame of the "select forest items" interaction (the forest editor's Select tool): hover in white, click = select (Ctrl adds, click in empty space clears), selection rectangle (Ctrl adds), drawing of the selection boxes (orange) and the transform gizmo. Restricted to items passing filterFn.

forest.desc: Forest object (nothing is done if nil)

updateInstantiateMode.desc: One frame of the "instantiate an item" interaction: raycast under the cursor, preview (sphere, the mesh's actual bounding box, face line; pivot cell in orange) and, on left click, creation of a cols x rows array of items of the itemDataId datablock (scale opts.scale, 1 by default), committed as ONE undoable action. Returns the list of items created on click, otherwise nil.

opts.desc: rayRange (default preference), cols/rows (1x1), colGap/rowGap (m, edge to edge on the mesh bounds, 0), yaw (degrees), alignToNormal, flipNormal, normalOffset (m, offset along the face), scale (1), afterCreate(item, forestData, index) (1-based index)

placementBasis.desc: Computes the placement basis of the array and the orientation of each item: unit (right, up, forward). Transform columns: X = right, Y = forward (window face), Z = up; the array advances along right (columns) and up (rows). World mode: world axes rotated by yawRad around Z. alignToNormal: the face follows the surface normal, the array lies in the surface plane and yawRad is a rotation in that plane. flip inverts the face.

listItemDatas.desc: Lists the ForestItemData datablocks filtered by name prefix (or internalName). matchPrefix = true: only those starting with prefix (parallax editor); false: all the others (forest editor). Sorted by name, case-insensitive.

matchPrefix.desc: true = keep the matching ones, false = the others

itemDataSelectable.desc: Shared mesh list row: datablock icon + full-width selectable, highlighted if selected. Returns true on click; the caller handles the selection state.

itemMatchesPrefix.desc: True if the name (or internalName) of the item's datablock starts with prefix.

isParallaxItem.desc: Convenience predicate for selection filters: is the item a parallax window (parallax_ prefix)?

isParallaxDataObject.desc: Same test on a ForestItemData datablock object (from scenetree.findObject), to filter the mesh palette.

returns.desc: true if name/internalName starts with parallax_

filterItems.desc: Returns a new list containing the items for which keep(item) is true (nil list = empty list).

unpackParallaxData.desc: Decodes the customData into (setId, emissive). setId is -1 if no parallax set is assigned.

packParallaxData.desc: Encodes (setId, emissive) into customData. setId < 0 or nil gives -1 (disabled; the C++ does not save customData < 0).
